$comment: The broker's local control protocol, as a fixture both languages read. Node: src/control-server.js and bin/handoff-admin.mjs, held against this file by test/control-protocol.test.js. Python (Hermes side, later slices): the drop control client. Nothing here is secret and nothing here is a credential.

transport.exchange: one request line out, one response line back, then the server closes

error_notes.invalid_request: A caller mistake: unknown op, missing or ill-typed field, oversized line, unsupported notice_platform. Never a statement about a handoff.
error_notes.unavailable: One body for missing, malformed, expired, consumed and lapsed. A content invariant, not a timing one: `await` blocks only for a live pending handoff and therefore leaks liveness to its local caller by construction.

create.summary: Mint one handoff and return its one-time URL.

ttl_seconds.note: Defaults to the broker's ttlSeconds (1800); must be > 0 and <= maxTtlSeconds (3600).

notice_platform.note: Opt-in. When present, the response also carries notice, notice_received and notice_expired. An unlisted value is refused with invalid_request and mints nothing.

response.handoff_id: 22 base64url characters; non-secret and safe to log
response.url: <base>/#<capability> — the capability rides in the fragment and appears nowhere else
response.notice: only when notice_platform was given: the waiting message, rendered for that platform
response.notice_received: only when notice_platform was given: the content the waiting message is edited into on submit; identical on every platform
response.notice_expired: only when notice_platform was given: the content it is edited into on lapse; identical on every platform

await.summary: Block on the submission event. Answers with a status and an id, never with the payload.

wait_ms.note: Defaults to 0. The broker never waits past the handoff's own expiry.

claim.summary: Consume the payload exactly once. The only op that returns plaintext.

wait_ms.note: Defaults to 0. When > 0, blocks on the submission event first, so nothing polls.

response.plaintext_b64: base64 of the payload bytes — transport encoding for the JSON line, not a protection measure

cli.rule: exit 0 means the payload is waiting: claim it. Any non-zero means do NOT claim.

exit_codes.1: transport failure — socket unreachable, request timed out, or the answer was malformed; the payload's fate is genuinely unknown
exit_codes.2: usage — a caller mistake, never a statement about the handoff
exit_codes.3: the broker answered unavailable: expired, consumed, or the wait lapsed
